# v1.1.0-dev.70 — Click the monitor you mean

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.69`.

The Display editor now shows your monitors the way Windows 11 does,
and edits one at a time.

## Pick From A Picture Of Your Desk

Windows reports "Generic PnP Monitor" for very nearly every display
ever made. So a stack of cards was asking you to tell three
identical-looking things apart from a position word.

There's a picture now. Your monitors, drawn to scale, sitting where
they actually sit, numbered:

```
 ┌──────────────┐┌───────┐
 │              ││       │
 │      1       ││   2   │
 │   PRIMARY    ││       │
 └──────────────┘└───────┘
 Select a display to change its settings.
```

Click one and its settings appear underneath. A monitor stood on
its end looks stood on its end. A small one next to a big one looks
small.

The editor opens on your primary display.

## The Others Aren't Hidden, Just Out Of The Way

A monitor this profile would change carries a dot in the corner of
its box. Putting the other cards away never puts away the fact that
they're set.

The summary at the top hasn't changed either. It still describes
every display the profile touches, selected or not, in plain words.

## Keyboard

The picker is one tab stop. Arrow keys move between displays and
wrap around at the ends.

## Under It

The geometry lives with the rest of the display maths rather than in
the window that draws it, which is what let it be tested properly.
Twenty-four checks cover keeping shapes right through rotation,
side-by-side and stacked arrangements, monitors sitting at negative
coordinates, and six different ways of asking for a layout that
can't be drawn. Every one of those would otherwise have produced a
box at an impossible position, which draws as a thin line rather
than anything that looks wrong.

The canvas takes the shape of your actual arrangement. Fitting a
desk into a fixed rectangle left it floating in empty space and made
a two-monitor setup look like it had gaps.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
